import json
import sys

raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
bundle = json.loads(raw[raw.index('{"ok"'):])["result"]
limit = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3000
print("stopping:", bundle["stopping_reason"], "gaps:", len(bundle["gaps"]))
for item in bundle["evidence"]:
    print("==", item["id"], item["path"], item["start_line"], item["end_line"])
    print(item["text"][:limit])

work_completed: (1) `lexical_fts` now has the columns `(text, ident, title)` and keeps `text`. `ident` holds the frontmatter `id`, the id at the start of the document's first heading and the id at the start of the section's heading. `title` holds the path, the document's first heading and the first line of the parent (a section heading or a `def` line). The index is still filled by the same incremental refresh by blob that `gov rebuild` calls, and the secrets filter still runs before any read. (2) `search` keeps `hits` exactly as before: every line that holds the exact string, in path and line order. It adds `ranked`: the chunks that hold the exact string first, in BM25 order (the boost), then up to 30 more chunks that match the question's words. The weights are `bm25(1.0, 10.0, 4.0)` for body, id and title, with `ORDER BY rank`. Words are matched one by one, not as a phrase (W2-M292), as whole tokens, case-folded and Porter-stemmed, with a short stopword list; an id in the question is matched as a phrase. This choice is recorded in the module docstring. (3) `search` never raises. A missing, empty or stale store gives its reason; an unreadable store or a git failure gives `unreadable`; a store built before W2-13 gives `stale`, and a refresh drops it and rebuilds it with the same digest. Any question is safe, including NUL characters, FTS5 syntax, quotes and lone surrogates. (4) `fusion.search` fuses `ranked`. (5) `gov retrieve`, given only a question (no `--ticket`, `--id` or `--continue`) whose id-shaped tokens all exist nowhere, returns `UNRESOLVED_IDS`, each id as an `UNRESOLVED` gap, and no evidence. "Exists nowhere" means no record has the id and no indexed line holds it as a whole token. If the lexical index is unavailable or the record graph cannot be read, nothing is decided there and the question is answered as before.
